chapters.title: What Do We Mean by Human Aggression?
chapters.observation: Defines aggression, injury, coercion, warfare, and atrocity through Morgan and Domesday while rejecting a universal violence scale.

chapters.title: Before States: Small Communities and the Archaeological Record
chapters.observation: Uses Jebel Sahaba and Crow Creek to separate bodily evidence, recurrent attack, social organisation, and ethical custody.

chapters.title: Cities, Kings, and the Invention of Organized War
chapters.observation: Reads Eannatum's stele as a conversion of force into durable claims about kingship, territory, religion, and administration.

chapters.title: Empires and the Management of Difference
chapters.observation: Contrasts Assyrian exemplary terror with Cyrus's accommodative rhetoric as distinct techniques of imperial rule.

chapters.title: Warriors, Cities, and Moral Order in the Americas
chapters.observation: Juxtaposes Moche sacrificial evidence with conquest-era testimony while carefully separating representation, practice, and mediation.

chapters.title: Frontiers, Faiths, and Political Fragmentation
chapters.observation: Moves among Temüjin, Lindisfarne, and Mongol communications to distinguish raiding, moral interpretation, coalition, and administration.

chapters.title: Steppe Powers and Connected Worlds
chapters.observation: Revisits Mongol rise and post-station proposals, clarifying conquest versus incorporation but duplicating much of Chapter 6.

chapters.title: States, Slavery, and the Atlantic World
chapters.observation: Shows how the Zong massacre became legally legible as insured loss within racialised Atlantic commerce.

chapters.title: Gunpowder, Bureaucracy, and Mass Mobilization
chapters.observation: Explains Swedish military capacity through farm obligations, crofts, equipment, routes, and prepared assembly.

chapters.title: Revolution and the Politics of the Crowd
chapters.observation: Treats the Bastille crowd as politically coordinated at several scales despite uncertainty about the decisive entry.

chapters.title: Colonial Rule and Resistance
chapters.observation: Connects Congo rubber coercion and Maji Maji cotton policy to testimony, revolt, scorched earth, famine, and conditional pardon.

chapters.title: Industrial War and the Civilian Population
chapters.observation: Keeps Davis's evidence of Armenian deportation and suffering distinct from unproven claims about industrial logistics.

chapters.title: Genocide, Total War, and Ideological Violence
chapters.observation: Reads Wannsee as coordination and the Einsatzgruppen trial as differentiated judgment of command and field responsibility.

chapters.title: After 1945: Deterrence and the Limits of the Supplied Record
chapters.observation: Reconstructs Cuban Missile Crisis restraint through public signals, private concessions, staged withdrawal, and communication limits.

chapters.title: What History Can and Cannot Explain
chapters.observation: Uses RTLM to connect dehumanising rhetoric, mass communication, institutions, and individual action without claiming monocausal explanation.
